title: Tata Steel partners with US company to make hydrogen from off-gases from plant
dek: Tata Steel is partnering with US firm Utility Global on a 10 tonnes-per-day facility to make high-purity hydrogen from steelmaking off-gases.
summary: Tata Steel has partnered with a US company to produce hydrogen from plant off-gases, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. The intended facility, based on Utility Global's H2Gen technology, will have a planned capacity of 10 tonnes per day (TPD) and will use off-gases from steelmaking to produce high-purity hydrogen. The excerpt does not give the location, cost or timeline.
keyFacts: Facility based on Utility Global's H2Gen technology
Planned capacity of 10 tonnes per day (TPD)
Uses steelmaking off-gases to produce high-purity hydrogen
whyItMatters: Converting process off-gases into hydrogen is one route to lowering emissions intensity without relying solely on renewable electrolysis.
implications: If successful, the approach could be of interest to other integrated producers seeking incremental decarbonisation, particularly as carbon border charges loom.
publisherExcerpt: The intended facility, based on Utility Global’s H2Gen technology, will have a planned capacity of 10 tonnes per day (TPD) and will use off-gases generated during the steelmaking process to produce high-purity hydrogen.
